blocks.text: Hadhrat Awf bin Maalik Ashja'ee (RA) Jokes with Rasulullaah ﷺ

Hadhrat Awf bin Maalik Ashja'ee (RA) reports, "I went to Rasulullaah ﷺ during the expedition to Tabook while he was in a (very small) leather tent. I greeted Rasulullaah ﷺ with Salaam and after he replied, I asked, 'May I enter?' When Rasulullaah ﷺ permitted me to enter, I asked, 'All of me, O Rasulullaah ﷺ?' Rasulullaah ﷺ replied, 'All of you.' I then entered."
Hadhrat Waleed bin Uthmaan bin Abu Aaliyah explains that Hadhrat Awf bin Maalik (RA) joked "All of me" because the tent was very small.[^1]
Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) and Hadhrat Abu Sufyaan (RA) Joke with Rasulullaah ﷺ

Hadhrat Ibn Abu Mulaykah (RA) narrates that when Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) only cracked a few jokes with Rasulullaah ﷺ, her mother said, "O Rasulullaah ﷺ! Many of our tribe's jokes come from the Kinaana tribe." "In fact," Rasulullaah ﷺ remarked, "this tribe is the subject of many of our jokes."[^2]

Hadhrat Abul Haytham reports from someone that he heard Hadhrat Abu Sufyaan bin Harb (RA) joking with Rasulullaah ﷺ in the house of his daughter Hadhrat Ummu Habeebah (RA) (who was one of Rasulullaah ﷺ's wives). Hadhrat Abu Sufyaan (RA) said, "By Allaah! As soon as I left you alone (stopped fighting you), all the Arabs also left you, otherwise the horned ones and hornless ones would all still be fighting because of you." Rasulullaah ﷺ smiled as he said, "You and what you say, O Abu Handhala."[^3]
The Sahabah (RA) throw Melons at each other and the Statement of Hadhrat Ibn Seereen about their Humour
Hadhrat Bakr bin Abdullaah says, "Although the Sahabah (RA) of Rasulullaah ﷺ used to (playfully) throw melons at each other, they were still the most resolute men when matters were serious."[^4]

Hadhrat Qurra narrates that he once said to Hadhrat Ibn Seereen, "Did the Sahabah (RA) joke and play?" Hadhrat Ibn Seereen replied, "They were just like other people. In fact, Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) used to say the following couplet in jest:
"He (is so miserly that) loves to drink wine from the money of his companions and dislikes to part with his own money"[^5]
Abu Dawood, as quoted in Al Bidaayah wan Nihaayah (Vol.6 Pg.46).
Zubayr bin Bakkaar and Ibn Asaakir, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.4 Pg.43).
